cells.tense: Right now you are standing where something you tended has come into its own, and it shows.
cells.act: trace the pattern across the last few times
cells.ask: Look back over the last few things you helped along and find the move you made in each — the same move, if it's there. Name it once, quietly, to nobody, and stop.
cells.core:
Something you've been bringing along is flowering, and you're not straining to make it shine. You kept at it while it was small, gave it what it needed and no more, and now the light coming off it is just what happened. When people ask what you did, you can give the plain version, because you know exactly what you did.

The next stretch is about seeing your own hand in it. Look back over the last few things you helped grow and find the move you made in each, the same move if it's there. Name it once, quietly, to nobody. When you can name the move, you can make it on purpose next time instead of noticing it only after it worked.
cells.sheetLine: You kept it small and it came up shining.
cells.verb: Following a light you can already see
cells.place: Where something young is being brought along

cells.tense: Somewhere ahead of you the thing you're bringing along is already lit, and you're holding that picture like a shield.
cells.act: wait until you know which part matters, then begin with that part
cells.ask: Choose something in your care and hold off on it until the part that needs you is clear. Let the not-knowing take a full day. Then do that part and nothing else.
cells.core:
The light you're aiming at sits somewhere ahead, and you keep pointing at it — how it will be once it's grown, what it will mean, how good it will look. That brightness is real, and it's steadying to hold. It also keeps you from seeing what's here today, which is smaller and less finished than the picture.

Slow down before you touch the next thing. Take something in your care and don't move on it until the part that needs you is clear; let the not-knowing take a full day. Then do that part only and leave the rest as it is. What you find in the waiting will be more accurate than what you'd have pushed forward.
cells.sheetLine: You're lighting the future to avoid the small room.

cells.tense: You are still standing past a door that closed while your hands were full with something else.
cells.act: give it what it needs today, not what it is scheduled for
cells.ask: Take something barely started and give it only what it needs today, at the size it's at now. Ask nothing back and make no plan for what it becomes.
cells.core:
Care has asked a lot of you and handed back little, more than once, and you've kept tending anyway — or you stopped and felt bad about that. Either way the cupboard where hope used to be is empty, and you're not sure it was naive to expect anything to come up.

There's one thing that won't ask much of you: take something barely started and give it what it needs today, at the size it's at now. Nothing ahead of that. No plan for what it becomes. Small enough that you could do it with the energy you have. That's all of it.
cells.sheetLine: Something small, today's needs only, nothing asked back.

cells.tense: The light's still coming off what you tend, and you are not counting yourself in it.
cells.act: hold your shape under the weight
cells.ask: When someone asks what you did or tries to hand the credit somewhere else, stay at your real size — not bigger, not smaller — and leave your part standing as it is.
cells.core:
Things grow near you and people notice, and when they ask how, you point at good timing, the soil, the kid's own nature. You'd say you just kept the thing alive. Keeping it alive was yours, and it goes unnamed even in your own head, which means you don't know when you've stopped and don't know when to start again.

Hold your own shape. When the credit comes around and someone tries to put it elsewhere, stay at your real size — not bigger, not smaller — and leave your part standing. You've been carrying this without flexing, and it can take a little more than you think.
cells.sheetLine: You kept it alive. That was your part.
